title: Simulation of a Boolean word scan
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let $v_0,v_F,v_T,r_1,r_2,n$ be states. Suppose the transitions from $v_0,v_F,v_T$ act according to the value word action, with the remembered last bit respectively absent, false, and true; suppose $r_1$ moves the input head left and enters $r_2$, while $r_2$ moves left and stays in $r_2$ when it reads a symbol, and moves right and enters $n$ at the right boundary. Assume none of these five states is a call state. For a configuration $c$, integer position $p$, Boolean word $x$, word $w$, and natural number $q$ satisfying $q+|w|=|x|+1$, assume that at every offset $k$ the symbol read at input position $q+k$ is the $k$-th bit of $w$. Starting at input position $q$ in state $v_0,v_F$, or $v_T$ according as the remembered bit is absent, false, or true, with register $r$'s head at $p$ and all other configuration data inherited from $c$, the run reaches the analogous configuration in state $n$ at input position $1$ if the last bit of $w$ (or the remembered bit when $w$ is empty) is not false; if that bit is false, it instead halts after appending a rejecting output bit, with register-head positions equal to those of $c$ except that register $r$ is at $p$. In either case, every earlier configuration is in a state with no call and has the same register-head positions, with register $r$ at $p$.
